entry.content:
D-Link M60 emDaemon MQTT Broker mosquitto.conf system hard-coded credentials
A vulnerability has been found in D-Link M60 1.12.B01. Impacted is the function system of the file /etc/emDaemon/mosquitto.conf of the component emDaemon MQTT Broker. Such manipulation leads to hard-coded credentials. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

Local privilege escalation to root in the DynamicCLI daemon via local world-writable control socket
The Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket (/tmp/dynamic_socket) without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.

entry.summary: Likely next · score 18/100. Nuclei template (http · medium): scannable at scale; Part of GitHub bulk release · Nov 11 (56); EPSS 0.93% · 61st pct · day 3, too new to trust; Medium 5.3 · network (v3.1)
entry.content:
vulnerability-operator: IDOR exposing vulnerability reports via unauthenticated Report Handler
vulnerability-operator scans SBOMs and Images for vulnerabilities. Prior to version 0.28.16, an unauthenticated information-disclosure vulnerability exposes all vulnerability scan reports served by the operator. The /report/ HTTP endpoint mounts a raw http.FileServer over the reports directory (default /reports) with no authentication, authorization, or middleware. Any client that can reach the operator's HTTP port (default 8080) can list and download every JSON vulnerability report, disclosing CVE IDs, affected package names/versions, and container image identifiers for every workload scanned in the cluster. This issue has been patched in version 0.28.16.

Printcart Store <= 2.13.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via nbu_crop_image 'url' Parameter
The Printcart Store – Web to Print Product Designer for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.13.2. This is due to the `nbu_crop_image` AJAX handler accepting a user-supplied `url` parameter that `Nbdesigner_IO::convert_url_to_path()` concatenates onto the uploads base directory without normalizing or stripping `../` sequences, and then deriving both the output directory and output file extension via `pathinfo()` from the same attacker-controlled path — with no `stripImage()` call before `writeImage()` is invoked. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to write attacker-controlled PHP content to arbitrary locations outside the uploads directory, resulting in remote code execution when the written file is subsequently requested. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the `nbdesigner_upload_popup_style` site option is set to `a` (Advanced Upload Popup), which causes the handler to be registered…

entry.title: CVE-2026-68982 · Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 72/100. 2 PoC repos (1 vetted), unverified, may be malware; Critical 9.8 · network (v3.1); Product in KEV (×1): Apache Airflow; CISA SSVC: total technical impact
entry.content:
Apache Airflow: CeleryExecutor: forged callback workloads run on Celery workers without workload-token validation
Apache Airflow's CeleryExecutor ran callback workloads (`ExecuteCallback`, used for deadline-alert callbacks) without validating the workload's authentication token. Anyone able to write to the Celery broker could enqueue a forged callback and execute arbitrary code on every CeleryExecutor worker, without Airflow credentials. Deployments using the CeleryExecutor are affected.
Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later, in which the worker claims the callback through the Execution API, validating the token, before running it.

entry.title: CVE-2026-86829 · Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 52/100. 1 PoC repo (1 vetted), unverified, may be malware; Product in KEV (×1): Apache Airflow; CISA SSVC: total technical impact; High 8.8 · network (v3.1)
entry.content:
Apache Airflow: Deserialization of task-controlled XCom values in the Scheduler during dependency evaluation
Apache Airflow's scheduler fully deserializes XCom values written by task code while evaluating task dependencies. A Dag author, who controls what a task writes to XCom, therefore controls data that is deserialized inside the scheduler process - a context the Airflow security model reserves for code installed by the Deployment Manager, above the worker-scoped execution capability a Dag author is documented to have. Deployments that treat Dag authors as less trusted than Deployment Managers are affected, and the scheduler must be evaluating a task dependency that reads a task-written XCom value. Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to version 3.4.0 or later, which restricts dependency evaluation to primitive XCom values.

When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.

entry.content:
SQL injection leading to privilege escalation
An unauthenticated SQL injection can occur on the front end of any site that uses craft.search to perform a search, allowing stacked query execution and enabling escalation to an administrator.
Note that this only affects MySQL/MariaDB.
Impact * SQL injection — The attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized, and because PDO runs with emulated prepares, stacked statements execute. This gives unauthenticated read and write access to the application database. * Privilege escalation to administrator — The write primitive was used to set the admin flag on user ID 1 in the users table, confirmed by reading the value back. Craft short-circuits its permission checks on this single column, so no further changes were needed. The same primitive can overwrite any account’s password hash.
Update to the patched versions (4.18.9 and 5.11.2) to get the fix.
